utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm glad you came in. Burning when you wee can have a few causes, so I'll ask a few questions to find the right treatment. Have you been needing to wee more often or urgently, and have you noticed any blood in your urine?
reply: It stings and burns, especially right at the end, just like my last UTI. I am going constantly, about every half hour, only a little bit comes out, and I have to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had any fever, shaking chills, pain in your back or sides, nausea or vomiting? Any pain low in your tummy?
reply: No, I haven't had any fevers or shivers and I feel fine apart from this, and there is nothing in my back except for a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. I am eating normally and haven't been sick, and it is just that low ache above my bladder with nothing else.

utterance: Any vaginal discharge, itching, sores, bleeding between periods or after sex, or pain during sex? When was your last period, and is there any chance you could be pregnant, including any missed pills?
reply: No, I haven't had any discharge or anything like that, and there is no bleeding between my periods or after sex, nor any pain during sex. My last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal, and I don't think I could be pregnant because I am on the pill and I don't miss it.

awards.label: Bleeding after sex or between periods
Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: When was your last urine infection, how was it treated, and did it fully clear? How many have you had in the past year?
reply: I only had one about two years ago, and that is it.

utterance: Do you remember which antibiotic you took then or whether a urine sample was tested? Have you taken any antibiotics recently?
reply: I don't remember which one I took or if it was tested, and I haven't had any antibiotics this year.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months

utterance: I ask everyone with these symptoms about sexual health because some infections can feel like a urine infection. Have you had a new sexual partner recently, do you use condoms, and have you or a partner ever had a sexually transmitted infection?
reply: Um, yeah, I have a boyfriend and we have been together about a year, just him, and we do not use condoms because I am on the pill.

utterance: Have you ever had a sexual health test or a sexually transmitted infection? Do you have any kidney or bladder problems, kidney stones, diabetes, or problems with your immune system?
reply: No, I have never had a sexual health test or a sexually transmitted infection, and I don't have any kidney or bladder problems, diabetes, or issues with my immune system.

utterance: Apart from your pill, are you taking any medicines or supplements, or have you tried anything for this? Do you have any medicine allergies?
reply: I only take my combined oral contraceptive pill, and I haven't tried anything else for this. No, I am not allergic to anything that I know of.

utterance: Your symptoms sound most like a bladder infection. With your permission I'll check your temperature and pulse, feel your tummy, and gently tap your back over your kidneys. I'd also like a urine sample to check for infection.
reply: Can't we just skip the checks and write the script? I really need to get back to work soon.

utterance: I understand you're in a hurry. These checks only take a couple of minutes and help make sure this isn't a kidney infection needing different treatment. We can keep this focused and get you back to work as soon as possible. Is that okay?
reply: All right, if it's quick, let's just get it done.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: The checks are reassuring, and your urine test supports a bladder infection. There are no signs of a kidney infection today. I'd like to check the urine for pregnancy too, as that changes which treatment is safest. Also, we routinely offer chlamydia and gonorrhoea screening to sexually active people your age, even without symptoms; would you like that today? A self-collected vaginal swab can be used.
reply: Oh, do we really need to do the pregnancy and STI tests too? I just want to get my antibiotics and head back to the cafe.

utterance: The sexual health screen is optional and can wait for another visit; I don't suspect it is causing these symptoms. The pill makes pregnancy very unlikely, but checking the urine you've already provided takes only minutes and helps us choose the antibiotic safely. Are you happy to do just that test now?
reply: Fine, if it is just a quick test and I can get my script, let's just do it.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Your pregnancy test is negative. This is an uncomplicated bladder infection. I've prescribed trimethoprim: one 300 mg tablet at night for three nights. Finish all three doses. It can cause nausea or a rash; seek urgent help for swelling or breathing difficulty. It doesn't directly reduce your pill's effectiveness, but vomiting or severe diarrhoea can—follow your pill's missed-pill advice if that happens.

Drink enough water to avoid dehydration; you don't need to force extra litres. Don't hold your urine, and you can take paracetamol according to the packet for pain. You can work if you feel well and can access the toilet.

You should start feeling better within 24–48 hours. If you're not clearly improving within 48 hours, or symptoms return after treatment, come back so we can send urine to the lab and review the antibiotic. If you develop fever, shaking chills, back or side pain, vomiting, or feel very unwell, seek urgent care the same day—go to emergency if severe. Those can mean infection has reached the kidneys. Any questions about the treatment?
reply: Oh good, no questions, just glad I can finally get my script and get back to work.
